neutral_facts.value: The accused, along with his son and companions, were present in front of a bank when the accused Vanshraj Yadav attacked the accused Ashfaque Ahmad by throwing a grenade. Subsequently, other accused persons started indiscriminate firing, resulting in the death of Ashfaque Ahmad on the spot and injuries to Razi Ahmad. Two accused persons were caught at the scene, and weapons, including a grenade, pistols, magazines, and a mobile phone, were recovered from their possession. One of the accused disclosed that the respondent Rajesh Vikram Singh and his brother had sent the accused persons to commit the murder of Ashfaque Ahmad. The motive was that the father-in-law of Ashfaque Ahmad was a witness in another criminal case against Rajesh Vikram Singh, in which he was eventually convicted. The High Court granted bail to the respondents, but the Supreme Court overturned this decision, finding that the High Court did not consider relevant material, including the criminal records of the respondents, the nature of the crime, and the presence of crucial eye witnesses.

quotes.text: The appeals are allowed, the impugned orders dated 23.09.2021, passed by the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench, Lucknow in Bail Application No. 624 of 2019 and Bail Application No. 4309 of 2019, granting regular bail to the private respondents, are hereby set aside.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the murder was a contract killing with a clear motive, and that the respondents were involved in a conspiracy to eliminate the victim. The case involved serious offenses under multiple IPC sections and the Explosive Substances Act, with evidence of recovered weapons and a motive linked to a previous criminal case against one of the respondents.

quotes.text: The murder of Ashfaque Ahmad took place in broad daylight. The occurrence has been witnessed by the appellant and two more eye witnesses. Two of the accused were nabbed at the spot. It was apparently a case of contract killing.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the High Court did not properly consider the relevant material when granting bail, and that the respondents had a criminal record but the case was not a clear-cut instance of misuse of bail. They also emphasized the need for the trial to proceed and that the High Court's order should not be overturned.

quotes.text: The High Court did not take into consideration the relevant material while granting bail to the private respondents.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the grant of bail should be based on a judicial assessment of the well-known parameters including the nature of the accusation, the severity of the punishment, the accused's criminal record, and the likelihood of tampering with evidence or obstructing justice.

quotes.text: The order granting bail should reflect the judicial application of mind taking into consideration the well-known parameters including: the nature of the accusation weighing in the gravity and severity of the offence.
